newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorians see output, veg fats as main ICCO issues.
newsitem.headline: Ivorians see output, veg fats as main ICCO issues.

text.p: Ivory Coast expects a meeting of the International Cocoa Organisation (ICCO) in London next week to focus on the use of non-cocoa vegetable fats in chocolate and on output targets needed to balance world supply and demand.
A statement from the Ivorian Commodities Ministry on Thursday said the two main issues would be -

"The re-examination of annual forecasts for world cocoa production and consumption before fixing production volumes needed to maintain the balance between supply and demand, a factor in price stabilisation."
"An examination... of a European Commission directive on the use of more than five percent vegetable fat other than cocoa butter in the manufacture of chocolate."
It said demand for cocoa in the European Union could fall by 200,000 to 250,000 tonnes a year at a cost of 300 billion CFA to producers if the directive was adopted.
Some industry sources say the fall in demand for cocoa would be much less drastic and some even predict a positive impact.
They say increased use of cheap vegetable fats like palm oil could boost cocoa use in warm regions by allowing manufacture of chocolate with a higher melting point than traditional recipes.
The statement said that Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze would represent Ivory Coast at the September 9-13 talks.
It said the Cocoa Producers' Alliance of origin countries planned to meet ahead of the ICCO session. --David Gault, Abidjan Newsroom +225 21 90 90
